To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
selective taxation on healthy and unhealthy food items has the potential to reduce the burden of CVD and nutrition related cancers.
the selective taxation of food commodities in Denmark could have a positive health effect.
the potential impact of selective taxation on the burden of disease is modest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of selective taxation to reduce the burden of CVD and nutrition related cancers.

the use of selective taxation as a health economic instrument to reduce disease burden from nutrition-related chronic diseases, and the health benefits of such an instrument in relation to the burden of disease.
the health benefits of a selective taxation of healthy food and unhealthy food commodities, and how these benefits are related to CVD and cancers, in particular IHD and nutrition related cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
selective taxation can be used as an instrument to improve public health and reduce the burden of CVD and cancer in the Danish population.
the health benefits of a selective tax on fats and a tax reduction of fruit and vegetables are moderate, and that a tax on sugar-sweetened beverages is of limited importance.
selective taxation can be a useful tool in the fight against CVD and nutrition related cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
selective taxation of healthy foods is an effective tool for public health policy.
selective taxation of healthy foods and unhealthy foods can be used as an economic instrument to improve the population's health, but that the effects of such taxation should not be overestimated.
the health benefits of a selective taxation policy in relation to CWD and nutrition-related cancers is limited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health benefits of taxation of unhealthy food are likely to be modest and that taxation of healthy foods is likely to be beneficial.
selective taxation of food commodities is not a panacea for all health problems.
the health effects of selective taxes are modest, and that a combination of taxes on different food groups is needed to obtain the largest health effects.
